newsitem.title: USA: Airlines settle suit on travel agent fees.
newsitem.headline: Airlines settle suit on travel agent fees.

text.p: Five of the nation's largest airlines have agreed to pay a total of $77 million to settle an antitrust lawsuit over caps on commissions paid to travel agents, the airlines and travel agents said Tuesday.

United Airlines, American Airlines, Delta Air Lines Inc. and Northwest Airlines Corp. agreed to pay $72 million to settle the antitrust suit claiming that major carriers had conspired to fix commissions paid to U.S. travel agents, Northwest said in a release issued on behalf of the airlines and travel agents.

Separately, Continental Airlines Inc., said it agreed to pay about $5 million, including its attorneys' fees, to settle its part of the case, which was brought in 1995 after airlines put limits on fees they pay to travel agents.
The latest settlements came days after a settlement was reached with USAir, according to an attorney for the travel agents. Trans World Airlines Inc. settled in May 1995.
The total amount of the settlements is $86 million, the release said.

The suit, filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota, claimed that seven major U.S. airlines conspired to fix and maintain the commissions paid to U.S. travel agents for domestic travel.

The suit was filed by the American Society of Travel Agents and 20 travel agents. The class action combined 14 separate lawsuits that were filed beginning February 1995, soon after the airlines imposed commission caps.
Previously, travel agents received a commission of 10 percent of the price of a ticket for U.S. travel.
Following the change, the carriers paid a fixed $25 commission for a domestic roundtrip ticket worth $250 to $500, and $50 for a ticket worth $500 or more.
The settlement announced Tuesday will be submitted for approval Thursday in U.S. District Court in Minnesota, the news release said.
The case had been set for trial to start Wednesday.
Continental, United, American, Delta and Northwest denied any wrongdoing and said they settled to avoid the risks and expenses of litigation.
The society of travel agents said the proceeds from the settlement would be distributed to travel agents.
